root.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted: Smyslov Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 dxc4 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3 g6

overview: After 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.e3 Black fianchettos with 4...g6 instead of the usual ...e6 and ...c5. White takes the pawn back with Bxc4, castles and builds with Nc3, Qe2 and e4; Black has ...Bg7, ...O-O and aims at ...c5 or ...c6/...b5. The game is a positional fight over the d4/e4 centre.

white_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn with Bxc4 and castle
Occupy the centre with e4 and Qe2/Rd1

black_ideas.idea: Develop the bishop on g7 and castle
Strike with ...c5 or ...c6 and ...b5 to challenge the centre
Trade pieces and fight against the d4/e4 pawns

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d4 and e3 against a fianchettoed Black bishop
Black queenside majority against White centre

character.notes: A fianchetto QGA where neither side takes early risks; play is manoeuvring around the centre.

gambit.notes: White regains the c4 pawn at once with Bxc4.

soundness.notes: A sensible Black set-up; no sign it is anything other than sound.

structure.notes: The c-pawn is gone, so White holds d4/e3 against a fianchetto and the centre is not locked.

approach.notes: A secondary line of the Queen's Gambit Accepted, played by some strong players.

level.notes: Needs a feel for the centre and the ...c5 break rather than many forcing lines.

character.reason: Positional play with neither side forced into risk.

structure.reason: QGA anchor is Open; White holds d4/e3 against the fianchetto with an open centre.

plans.reason: Black fianchettos, White holds the larger centre.
